assays.assay_description: Manual counting of head twitches after i.p. psilocin or mushroom extracts. Two experimental variants collapsed: (1) dose-response 0.25–2 mg/kg, head twitches observed after 10 min (n=150); (2) 1 mg/kg hallucinogen given 15 min before 5-HTP 200 mg/kg, observation periods of 10 and 20 min (n=50). Apparatus not described.

time_to_assay.evidence: The number of head twitches was observed after 10 min. / tested mushroom extracts and pure psilocin (at dose 1 mg/kg) were injected 15 min before 5-HTP ... The observation period was 10 and 20 min.

sample_size.evidence: In the behavioral test, 150 mice were used to investigate the administrated dose and 50 mice in tests concerning a potency of drug-induced hallucinogenic effect. ... In control groups of ten mice

outcomes.summary: Psilocin and both mushroom extracts dose-dependently induced head twitches (0.25–2 mg/kg), with a maximum at 1 mg/kg and fewer twitches at higher doses; psilocin produced the most twitches, extracts a similar effect despite lower psilocin content. In the 5-HTP (200 mg/kg) experiment, psilocin produced ~60% fewer head twitches than the full agonist 5-HTP, and the extracts ~45% (Ph. cyanopus) and ~30% (P. semilanceata) fewer, interpreted as partial agonism at 5-HT2A.
outcomes.statistics: one-way ANOVA with post hoc Bonferroni; * p < 0.05, ** p < 0.01, *** p < 0.001 compared to the control group
outcomes.evidence: Dose of 1 mg/kg elicited the maximal number of head twitches in mice. Further increasing of the amounts of hallucinogens decreased the number of observed head twitches. ... The application of pure psilocin gave significantly lower head-twitch response (about 60% lower) compared to the effect of full agonist (5-HTP)
